data.name: Project Process
table: Describe the invention's effects, how it operates, what kind of energy it requires, and the specific benefits it provides. The Game Master has final say on whether a given invention is feasible in your circumstances.

If an invention is complex enough — such as a magitech motorcycle equipped with a cannon, acting as both a vehicle and a weapon — the Game Master is free to split the Project into two or more separate inventions, each requiring its own individual development process.

By consulting the area, potency, and uses tables, the GM determines the invention's total cost in materials, to be paid immediately. For inventions of medium or higher potency, the Game Master also describes a necessary special ingredient or material. This item cannot simply be purchased and should become the focus of one or two sessions.

You may negotiate a terrible flaw with the Game Master — perhaps the invention must be recharged at regular intervals, is unreliable, cumbersome, or extremely loud. This flaw reduces the total cost of the Project by 25%.

To complete the Project, you must reach an amount of progress equal to one for every 100 zenit of material costs (minimum one progress required). At the end of each day, the Project will advance as follows: +1 progress for every Player Character who worked on the Project today. +1 extra progress for every Player Character with one or more levels in the Tinkerer Class who worked on the Project today.

Once the required amount of progress is reached, the invention is created! If you can generate more progress in a day than what is currently needed to complete the Project, you may have it ready within a few hours instead.

data.name: Potency Table
table: Provide light, transport people or cargo on land or water, obtain some limited form of protection.
Travel underwater, contain a spell, relay sound or speech, perform a specific operation in place of the inventor, provide short-term energy.
Fly, alter the nature of an area for a short time, cancel the effects of a spell, possess minor intelligence, fight alongside the inventor, provide long-term energy, capture or immobilize the target.
Alter the nature of an area for a long time, contain the power of a demon, prevent a catastrophe, possess a full intelligence and personality.

data.name: Area Table
table: The effects of the invention may affect...
A human-sized creature, a door, a tree, or a weapon.
A group of human-sized creatures, a large creature, a small clearing, a room, a railway car, or a hut.
A crowd, a small forest, an airship or galleon, a castle hall, a house, or a giant creature.
A fortress, a lake, the top of a mountain, a village, or a city block.

data.name: Uses Table
table: Can never be used again unless the inventor creates a different copy of it.
Remains available for multiple uses in different situations.

data.name: Project Design Rules
table: Avoid creating inventions that grant Immunity to physical damage.
If an invention has mixed effects, such as granting Resistance to a damage type and dealing damage, it should be split into multiple Projects (see step 2).
To determine the amount of damage or healing granted by an invention, use the values corresponding to the current level of its inventor from the damage amounts table.

data.name: Optional: Limited Resting Scenes
data.description:
Once the group plays a `resting scene` (Core Rulebook, page 91), they cannot do so again until at least one of the following events has happened (but they can still rest to heal HP, MP, and status effects):

- One or more Player Characters have gained levels.

- One or more Player Characters have `Sacrificed` themselves.

- One or more Villains have escalated.

Bonds can still be created via opportunities (Core Rulebook, page 41).

data.name: Optional: Cinematic Projects
data.description:
Replaces steps 5 and 6 of the standard Project process (Core Rulebook, page 134). Also ignore the rules for hiring helpers (page 137); the Tinkerer's `Visionary` Skill changes when using this rule (see Tinkerer class data).

**Quick Projects.** Outside conflict scenes, a Player Character with access to Projects can spend a few seconds to assemble a consumable invention of minor or medium potency with an individual, small, or large area. The group must have enough materials and/or zenit to cover the Project's cost immediately, and must also consume a special ingredient or material even if potency is minor. Characters may directly spend zenit rather than procuring materials first.

**Slow Projects.** Once per rest, a group that includes one or more Player Characters with access to Projects can assemble a single invention with a material cost equal to or lower than 1000 zenit. Increase this limit by `【SL × 200】` from the highest `Visionary` Skill Level in the group, by 1000 if resting in a place that facilitates the Project, and double it if adapting or repairing an existing object (the object does not count as a special ingredient for medium+ potency). Only one slow Project per rest, regardless of how many PCs have Projects.
